reason: 'A new and greater temple' casts the Church as the antitype of Israel's temple; it is a typological title with no prefigure/fulfil wording, so preparatory is the ceiling and is acceptable. The same prayer's sharper figure (the sons of Levi as 'ministers of your tabernacle' set beside the threefold ministry, i.e. Levites to deacons/Holy Orders) was not extracted.
'Considers Melchizedek... as a prefiguration of the priesthood of Christ' is explicit wording, and Christ the High Priest is the exact antitype ('high priest after the order of Melchizedek').

'Everything that the priesthood of the Old Covenant prefigured finds its fulfillment in Christ Jesus' is explicit, and the paragraph's subject is Christ's unique priesthood, so Christ the High Priest is the right precision.

'The priest of the old law was a figure of Christ' is explicit; in context (Christ as 'high priest of the redemptive sacrifice', 'source of all priesthood') the antitype is Christ as High Priest, not the NT minister, who only 'acts in the person of Christ'.
§1605 expounds Gen 2:18-24 (the 'helpmate', 'one flesh') as the Creator's plan 'in the beginning', so it teaches about the first marriage; no typological link is stated here.
§1610 speaks directly of 'the pedagogy of the old law' and 'the law given to Moses' on marriage and divorce; teaches-only is right.

§1611 teaches that the prophets saw the covenant with Israel 'in the image of exclusive and faithful married love'; it ties that image to a deeper understanding of marriage, not to an NT antitype, so teaches-only is right.

§1611 names the Song of Solomon and reads it as human love that reflects God's love; no NT antitype, so teaches-only is right. The text concerns the Song's love as such, not the ecclesial reading in this Type's description, but it is the nearest existing Type.

'Had prepared the way for the new and everlasting covenant' is exact preparatory wording, and that covenant is described nuptially (the Son 'has united to himself... all mankind saved by him', 'the wedding-feast of the Lamb'), so Christ's union with the Church is a fair antitype. Covenantal follows the text's own word 'covenant', though other christ-church rows are filed Ecclesial.

The link is real: Paul applies Gen 2:24, which §1605 identifies with the Creator's plan for the first couple, to 'Christ and the Church'. But 'a great mystery... in reference to' is not prefigure/figure/type wording, so explicit overstates it; read with §1605 it is synthesized.

cand_id: c1642:new:nuptial covenant god and israel>new:matrimony sacrament marriage
reason: 'Just as of old God encountered his people... so our Savior... now encounters Christian spouses through the sacrament of Matrimony' is an analogy between the two economies with no prepare/fulfil wording. The link to Matrimony stands only with §1612 (the nuptial covenant 'prepared the way') and §1617 (marriage as 'the sacrament of the covenant of Christ and the Church'), so synthesized.

The Beatitudes 'fulfill the promises by ordering them no longer merely to the possession of a territory, but to the Kingdom of heaven': the land is the concrete figure transposed, so preparatory holds. Borderline only because 'fulfill' grammatically attaches to the promises (spoken words); the cross-referenced §1820 ('heaven as the new Promised Land') confirms the land itself is meant.
'Heaven as the new Promised Land' is a typological title (like 'the new Adam') with no prefigure/figure/type wording, so explicit is too strong; preparatory is the ceiling.
'Revealed his Law to them, thus preparing for the coming of Christ' is preparatory wording with the Law as the preparing reality and Christ as the one prepared for.

§1963 describes the Law's nature and role ('first stage on the way to the kingdom', it 'prepares and disposes... for conversion and faith'); that is a pedagogical function for Israel and Christians alike, not a type-to-antitype link, so teaches-only is right.

'It prophesies and presages the work of liberation from sin which will be fulfilled in Christ', followed by 'images, "types," and symbols', is explicit foreshadowing wording; the Law is an institution, not a spoken oracle, so the prophecy exclusion does not apply.

The quoted 'preparation for the Gospel' is preparatory, but the same paragraph says the Law 'provides the New Testament with images, "types," and symbols for expressing the life according to the Spirit' (the New Law, §§1965-1966), which is explicit type wording for this very pair. Use that sentence as the quote.
'The Law of the Gospel "fulfills," refines, surpasses, and leads the Old Law to its perfection' is fulfilment wording for the same pair; preparatory is right.
'The Law of the Gospel fulfills the commandments of the Law' supports preparatory. Note this is the moral law brought to fullness ('far from abolishing or devaluing'), not a figure passing away.
In-brief restatement of §1964: 'a preparation for the Gospel' is exact preparatory wording.
'Fulfills and surpasses the Old Law and brings it to perfection' is fulfilment wording; preparatory is right.

In the Augustine quotation God's seventh-day rest was 'to foretell... that... we shall also rest in you on the sabbath of eternal life'; what foretells is an event, not a spoken oracle, so 'foretell' functions as foreshadow and explicit is defensible (cf. Heb 4:4-10). Antitype and category are right.
'Rediscover it in the person of his Master who is its perfect fulfillment' names Christ himself as the Law's fulfilment; preparatory and Christological are right.

§2056 says only that the Decalogue's 'full meaning will be revealed' in the New Covenant: a statement about understanding, with no prepare/fulfil/figure wording. The Law-to-Gospel link holds only when read with §§1968 and 2053-2055, so synthesized at most; it adds nothing the stronger rows lack.
'Images that pointed symbolically toward salvation by the incarnate Word' is explicit figure wording, the bronze serpent is named, and Christ ('the incarnate Word') is the antitype the text gives.

The text names 'the cherubim' among the images that 'pointed symbolically toward salvation by the incarnate Word', so the explicit link to Christ is in the text, unusual as it is; listed with the ark, the cherubim of the mercy seat are the right precision.
'The ark of the covenant' is named among the images that 'pointed symbolically toward salvation by the incarnate Word'; explicit and Christological are right.
§2169 recalls the sabbath's grounding in creation (Exod 20:11); teaches-only is right.
Here 'the Lord's day' means the sabbath, as the quoted Deut 5:15 shows ('to keep the sabbath day'), so the Type is the Sabbath, not Sunday; teaches-only is right.
'God entrusted the sabbath to Israel to keep as a sign of the irrevocable covenant' teaches about the Sabbath itself; teaches-only is right.
Jesus' 'authentic and authoritative interpretation' of the sabbath law; no type-to-antitype link is stated, so teaches-only is right.

§2174 defines the Lord's Day and its symbolism ('eighth day... symbolizes the new creation'); teaches-only is right. The first day of creation and the day of the Resurrection ('recalls the first creation', with Justin) is at most a synthesized link and was not extracted.

'Sunday fulfills the spiritual truth of the Jewish sabbath' is fulfilment wording, so preparatory; 'prefigured' in the next sentence has 'worship under the Law' as subject and 'some aspects of Christ' as object, not the Lord's Day. That sentence is itself a missed explicit claim: ceremonial-law -> christ (Christological).

'Sunday worship fulfills the moral command of the Old Covenant, taking up its rhythm and spirit' supports preparatory for Sabbath to Lord's Day; as in §1968 it is a moral command fulfilled rather than a figure, but the label rule holds.

Sound and needed: §§2174-2176 make the day itself, not the Resurrection event (the-resurrection) or the Eucharist celebrated on it (§2177), the fulfilment of the sabbath. The name follows the Catechism's 'the Lord's Day', and Acts 20:7 and Rev 1:10 are apt.

Distinct from christ-church (what marriage signifies, §1617) and adam-and-eve (the OT marriage); a plain sacrament name matching 'Holy Orders' and 'Eucharist', with a description true to §1617 and Eph 5:25-32.
'Typos tou Patros' makes the bishop a living image of God the Father; no OT figure or NT fulfilment is involved.
Ignatius's 'the bishop as the image of the Father' is the same image-of-God language as §1549, not OT-to-NT typology.
Apostolic transmission of the Spirit by the imposition of hands; no OT figure is named.
Apostolic succession and priests as co-workers of the bishops; no OT figure is named.

'After the image of Christ, the supreme and eternal priest' and 'true priests of the New Testament' imply a contrast with the old priesthood but name no OT figure; the explicit link is already carried by §§1544 and 1548.
Byzantine ordination prayer (altar, sacrifices, bath of rebirth); no OT figure is named.
Spousal love as 'an image of the absolute and unfailing love with which God loves man' is creation theology, not an OT figure fulfilled in an NT reality.
'Finds its fulfillment in the two becoming one flesh' concerns marital consent and its consummation, not an OT-to-NT link.

'What was done there prefigured some aspects of Christ' is explicit wording with Christ as object; its subject is 'worship under the Law', i.e. the cult, which §2175-2176 set apart from the moral command, so ceremonial-law is the right precision (the-mosaic-law too broad, ot-sacrifices too narrow).
